title: How Long Would You Last in Death Valley in July Without Water? #shorts
situation: DEATH VALLEY IN JULY, NO WATER
description_hook: You are stranded in Death Valley on a July afternoon that averages 116 °F, with no water at all. The clock starts now.

beats.say: How long would you last in Death Valley in July without water? An average July afternoon is 116 °F. The ground can hit 201 °F.
beats.img: a lone human silhouette seen from behind on a cracked white salt flat under a blinding midday sun, heat shimmer rippling over distant bare mountains

beats.text: 1 GALLON A DAY. YOU HAVE NONE
beats.say: The park says drink at least one gallon of water a day. You have none.
beats.img: an empty clear plastic water bottle lying on its side in pale desert sand, harsh overhead sunlight casting a short sharp shadow

beats.say: You walk for help. You sweat up to 2 litres an hour. Past about 5% fluid loss, your head pounds.
beats.img: a small figure from behind trudging along an empty desert road that vanishes into wavy heat haze, golden dunes on both sides

beats.say: At about 8-10% loss, you're weak, dizzy, and close to fainting.
beats.img: a tilted blurry view of rippled sand dunes and a white-hot sky, as if seen by someone about to collapse, colors washed out by glare

beats.say: Then heatstroke. Your core passes 104 °F and sweating may stop. It can hit 106 °F within 10 to 15 minutes.
beats.img: a glowing thermal-style outline of a human body slumped on a rocky desert slope, its core burning bright red against dark orange ground

gumi.say: Gumi's odds: two percent. This valley officially recorded 134 °F. Bring the gallon.
